- This is a day-2 lifecycle test on one enrolled authority and two clients. It does not cover a full site, replicas/failover, real power loss, or naturally occurring packet loss. Native faults are deterministic external process/transport faults.
- The machine closure contains 41 files, 60 unresolved ambient/Ansible dependencies and two external inputs. This is exact-candidate evidence with explicit fingerprints, not an automatic source/base-change reuse certificate. Execution-affecting changes require new validation.
- The formal profile deliberately retains ordinary Ansible host_vars canonical identity while the Go provider/hosts.yml mapping is absent. A completely unmapped effective inventory still reaches the pre-existing SSH guard refusal; this PR does not change that guard. Host-vars/external provider configuration are not newly claimed to be historically bound by InventoryRevision.
- The fixed native execution/read-only continuation and the negative control have explicitly separate profiles. Finalization legitimately removes the retiring inventory/host-vars metadata; immutable input copies and actual before/after hashes remain retained. No unchanged-all-workspace claim is made.
- Earlier `311629de8581f7d10101d2fba2186a04f1347401` native faults and `8a84a2111196b527265ff75561dedc6f2d50ce06` fresh-fixture main retain their historical attribution. Older unknown/ABA/service-gate/later-publication supplements tested `1eb9f2275612f469366662443d1f26fce38937d6` / tree `07745427003b11cb9f9d5e31bfccea0aa8d56d48`, binary `89e9aedb08e290f232e368038f686f73c1df5876676fcf9ca3b2444ae950648e`; they were not rerun as e10f4672 arms. Their provenance and limits remain in the [previous record](https://github.com/kjelly/pilot/blob/7d722f46ac4635c70793d3fb50d16b0dec4a59ff/docs/evidence/gateway-scope-retirement/issue-227.md), without cross-cohort equality claims.
- Captured outputs and the public diff were scanned for known admin/DM values and retained client private-key segments with no hits; the earlier pre-teardown scan also covered all four SSH key files. The native TLS key/PIN stayed inside the disposable server, and proxy logs contain no RPC bodies or authorization headers. This does not claim arbitrary secret-encoding detection.
